metadata.description: Azure region for everything in this deployment.
Prefix for the storage account. Lowercase alphanumeric, 3-14 chars - a random suffix gets appended.
Prefix stuck on the front of each export name. Defaults to namePrefix.
Tags applied to every resource this template creates.
Pin this to a fixed RFC3339 timestamp on redeploys so the export schedule windows do not churn. Leave alone for a first deploy.
MCA billing account ID. Used to build the billing profile scope path.
MCA billing profile ID - the scope every export runs against.
Create a new managed identity for the export script, or point at one that already exists.
Resource ID of a user-assigned managed identity that already holds the billing profile grant. Required when identityMode is existing.
Name for the managed identity when identityMode is create. Blank falls back to mi-<namePrefix>-exports.

Create the cost management exports. Leave false on the first pass of a create-identity deploy - the new identity has no billing permission yet, so the export script would fail. Grant it, then redeploy with this on.
FOCUS dataset schema version for the exports.
File format for every export. Parquet is smaller and faster to query; Csv is easier to eyeball.
Compression applied at delivery. snappy pairs with Parquet, gzip with Csv, or none.
Split large exports into multiple files with a manifest. Keep true for anything above a trivial spend.
OverwritePreviousReport keeps one current file set per month. CreateNewReport appends a new timestamped drop each run.
How far out to set the recurrence end date on the scheduled exports.
How far back the one-time export reaches when the explicit dates are not set. One day by default, 31 max.
Start of the one-time export window, UTC (e.g. 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z). Empty falls back to onetimeLookbackDays.
End of the one-time export window, UTC. Empty uses the deployment anchor date. Window cannot exceed a calendar month.
Blob container the exports get written into.
Storage account replication. LRS is usually fine since Azure can regenerate export data.
Turn the storage account into ADLS Gen2. Set true if Synapse/Databricks/Fabric will read the exports directly.
Optional public IP/CIDR allowlist. Empty list leaves the account open to all networks (still auth-gated).
Object IDs granted Storage Blob Data Reader on the export storage - users, groups, or service principals doing reporting.
Emit a read-only container SAS as a template output for tools that cannot use Entra auth.
Lifetime in days of the generated reader SAS.
Create a VNet, private DNS zone, and a blob private endpoint for the export storage. Also flips the storage firewall to Deny by default.
Build a new VNet/subnet for the private endpoint, or drop it into one that already exists.
VNet name. The one to create, or the existing one to use.
Resource group holding the existing VNet. Ignored when vnetMode is create.
Create the privatelink.blob.core.windows.net zone, or use one that already exists. A VNet can only be linked to one zone of a given name, so pick existing if the target VNet already has one.
Resource ID of an existing privatelink.blob.core.windows.net zone. Required when privateDnsZoneMode is existing.
Address space for the private endpoint VNet.
Subnet the private endpoint NIC lands in.
CIDR for the private endpoint subnet. Must sit inside vnetAddressSpace.
Deploy the Data Factory mover half. Set false to stand up cost management exports only.
Site name - drives the ADF resource names and the destination container on the customer account.
Customer storage account name the exports get mirrored into.
SAS token for the customer storage account. Needs rwdlac on blob service.
Daily trigger run time, HH:mm in timeZone.
Monthly trigger run time, HH:mm in timeZone.
Day of month the monthly trigger fires.
Integer N used in (today - N) to work out which month folder to mirror. With N=5, runs on the 1st-5th still target last month.
Windows time zone ID the triggers and the pipeline date math run in.
RG holding the existing VNet. Ignored when vnetMode is create.
Resource ID of an existing privatelink.blob.core.windows.net zone. Only read when privateDnsZoneMode is existing.
Changing this re-runs the script. Wired to the deployment anchor.

properties.scriptContent:
set -euo pipefail
API="2025-03-01"
BASE="https://management.azure.com${SCOPE}/providers/Microsoft.CostManagement/exports"

# one-time export window sanity check - the API caps a Custom timeframe at a
# calendar month and silently does odd things past that.
FROM_S=$(date -u -d "$ONETIME_FROM" +%s)
TO_S=$(date -u -d "$ONETIME_TO" +%s)
if [ "$TO_S" -le "$FROM_S" ]; then
  echo "ERROR: onetime window must run forwards ($ONETIME_FROM -> $ONETIME_TO)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
if [ $(( TO_S - FROM_S )) -gt 2678400 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: onetime window can't be longer than 31 days" >&2
  exit 1
fi

# put_export <key> <timeframe> <recurrence|""> <status> <rootFolder> <description>
put_export() {
  key="$1"; timeframe="$2"; recurrence="$3"; status="$4"; folder="$5"; desc="$6"
  name="${EXPORT_PREFIX}-${key}"

  definition=$(jq -n --arg tf "$timeframe" --arg dv "$DATASET_VERSION" \
    '{type:"FocusCost", timeframe:$tf, dataSet:{granularity:"Daily", configuration:{dataVersion:$dv}}}')

  # timePeriod only goes on the Custom (one-time) export
  if [ "$timeframe" = "Custom" ]; then
    definition=$(echo "$definition" | jq --arg f "$ONETIME_FROM" --arg t "$ONETIME_TO" \
      '. + {timePeriod:{from:$f, to:$t}}')
  fi

  # One-time exports take status and NOTHING else - the API rejects a
  # recurrence member even when it's null, so we leave the keys off entirely.
  if [ -z "$recurrence" ]; then
    schedule=$(jq -n --arg s "$status" '{status:$s}')
  else
    schedule=$(jq -n --arg s "$status" --arg r "$recurrence" --arg f "$SCHEDULE_FROM" --arg t "$SCHEDULE_TO" \
      '{status:$s, recurrence:$r, recurrencePeriod:{from:$f, to:$t}}')
  fi

  body=$(jq -n \
    --arg loc "$EXPORT_LOCATION" --arg d "$desc" --arg fmt "$EXPORT_FORMAT" \
    --arg cm "$COMPRESSION_MODE" --argjson pd "$PARTITION_DATA" --arg dob "$DATA_OVERWRITE" \
    --arg sa "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT_ID" --arg c "$CONTAINER_NAME" --arg rf "$folder" \
    --argjson def "$definition" --argjson sched "$schedule" \
    '{
      identity: {type:"SystemAssigned"},
      location: $loc,
      properties: {
        exportDescription: $d,
        format: $fmt,
        compressionMode: $cm,
        partitionData: $pd,
        dataOverwriteBehavior: $dob,
        definition: $def,
        deliveryInfo: {destination: {type:"AzureBlob", resourceId:$sa, container:$c, rootFolderPath:$rf}},
        schedule: $sched
      }
    }')

  echo "PUT $name (root=$folder, timeframe=$timeframe, recurrence=${recurrence:-none})"
  az rest --method put --url "${BASE}/${name}?api-version=${API}" \
    --headers "Content-Type=application/json" --body "$body" > "/tmp/${name}.json"

  # principalId is sometimes not on the PUT response yet, so poll the GET
  pid=$(jq -r '.identity.principalId // empty' "/tmp/${name}.json")
  tries=0
  while [ -z "$pid" ] && [ "$tries" -lt 10 ]; do
    sleep 5
    az rest --method get --url "${BASE}/${name}?api-version=${API}" > "/tmp/${name}.json" || true
    pid=$(jq -r '.identity.principalId // empty' "/tmp/${name}.json")
    tries=$((tries+1))
  done
  if [ -z "$pid" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: no managed identity principalId came back for $name" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "$pid" >> /tmp/principals.txt
}

: > /tmp/principals.txt

# All three are FocusCost - only the timeframe and schedule differ. The one-time
# one has an inactive schedule so it never fires on its own, you kick it off with
# Run now in the portal or the Execute API.
put_export "focus-onetime" "Custom"       ""        "Inactive" "focus-onetime" "One-time FOCUS cost and usage details"
put_export "focus-daily"   "MonthToDate"  "Daily"   "Active"   "focus-daily"   "Daily FOCUS cost and usage details, month to date"
put_export "focus-monthly" "TheLastMonth" "Monthly" "Active"   "focus-monthly" "Monthly FOCUS cost and usage details for last month"

jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))' /tmp/principals.txt \
  | jq '{principalIds: .}' > "$AZ_SCRIPTS_OUTPUT_PATH"

echo "done - $(wc -l < /tmp/principals.txt) exports created"

metadata.description: Full prefix under the source container the daily trigger mirrors, e.g. focus-daily/cgcm-focus-daily
Full prefix under the source container the monthly trigger mirrors, e.g. focus-monthly/cgcm-focus-monthly

Private endpoint subnet the export storage sits behind. Non-empty flips the factory into managed vnet mode - same test ADF.ps1 did on vnetSubnetId. ADF's own managed private endpoint lives in its managed vnet, not in this subnet; this is a mode flag, not an attachment point.
